words.meaning: Worship of idols or false gods; the practice of worshipping images or objects as deities.
words.example: The people of Noah were deeply involved in idolatry, worshipping statues instead of the One God.

words.meaning: The practice of living in a religious community separated from the world, often involving self-denial.
words.example: Christian monks adopted monasticism, withdrawing from society to devote themselves to prayer.

words.meaning: A violation of a law, command, or moral code; a sin or offence.
words.example: Noah warned his people repeatedly about their transgressions, but they refused to listen.

words.meaning: A severe flood; an overwhelming quantity of anything.
words.example: The deluge that Noah warned of would cover the entire earth and destroy all living things.

words.meaning: A solemn agreement or promise between God and a person or group.
words.example: God made a covenant with Ibrahim that his descendants would be blessed as a righteous nation.

words.meaning: Having unlimited power; all-powerful.
words.example: The Prophet reminded his people that the omnipotent God could see all their deeds.

words.meaning: The action of regretting or feeling sorry for past misdeeds and resolving to change.
words.example: The door of repentance remains open for those who sincerely turn back to God.

words.meaning: The act of rising from the dead; revival after death on the Day of Judgement.
words.example: The Prophet taught that every soul will face resurrection and be held accountable for its deeds.

words.meaning: Firmly determined and unwavering in purpose or belief.
words.example: Ibrahim remained steadfast in his faith despite the hostility of his entire nation.

words.meaning: Involving or resembling a miracle; extraordinary and seemingly impossible.
words.example: The miraculous splitting of the moon was shown to the disbelievers as a sign.

words.meaning: Assistance and support in times of hardship and distress.
words.example: The believers called upon God for succour when they were persecuted in Makkah.

words.meaning: Causing or deserving strong dislike or hatred; morally repugnant.
words.example: The practices of the idolaters were abhorrent to the monotheistic prophets.

words.meaning: A change of circumstances or fortune, typically one that is unwelcome.
words.example: The vicissitudes of life tested the patience and faith of every prophet.

words.meaning: Gentle, kindly, and harmless in nature or effect.
words.example: The benign countenance of the Prophet brought comfort to all who stood before him.

words.meaning: The act of bringing under domination or control; the state of being forced to obey.
words.example: Pharaoh sought the subjugation of the Children of Israel through tyranny and oppression.

words.meaning: Patient self-control; restraint and tolerance.
words.example: The Prophet showed great forbearance towards his enemies, never seeking revenge.

words.meaning: A divine communication or message revealed by God to His prophets.
words.example: The first revelation came to the Prophet in the Cave of Hira through the angel Jibreel.

words.meaning: Eternal damnation or ruin; complete loss or destruction.
words.example: Those who rejected the prophets were warned of perdition in the Hereafter.

words.meaning: An act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone, especially in a play.
words.example: The Prophet would often engage in soliloquy during his nightly prayers in the mosque.

words.meaning: A gesture or act of deep respect or submission; a bow or prostration.
words.example: The companions made obeisance to the Prophet as a mark of their reverence and love.

words.meaning: A cause of great trouble or suffering; a trial or hardship.
words.example: The early Muslims endured severe tribulations before their migration to Madinah.

words.meaning: Conducive to success; favourable and promising.
words.example: The Prophet was born on an auspicious night that the Arabs considered sacred.

words.meaning: To follow a winding course; to wander aimlessly.
words.example: The caravan meandered through the desert, following the ancient trade route to Sham.

words.meaning: Fearless and adventurous.
words.example: The intrepid companions feared no enemy and faced every battle with unwavering courage.

words.meaning: To formally abolish a law, right, or treaty.
words.example: The new revelation did not abrogate the earlier commandments but completed them.

words.meaning: Fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing; clearly expressing or indicating something.
words.example: The eloquent words of the Prophet moved even his bitterest enemies to tears.

words.meaning: Courage and strength in the face of pain or adversity.
words.example: The companions showed remarkable fortitude during the years of persecution in Makkah.

words.meaning: To regard with great respect or reverence.
words.example: The Muslims venerated the Prophet above all other human beings.

words.meaning: Very generous or forgiving, especially towards a rival or less powerful person.
words.example: The magnanimous character of the Prophet was shown when he forgave the people of Makkah.

words.meaning: To make something continue indefinitely; to preserve from extinction.
words.example: The Prophet instructed his companions to perpetuate the teachings of Islam for all generations.

words.meaning: Raised to a position of great power or honour; of high rank or status.
words.example: The exalted status of the Prophet is recognised by Muslims throughout the world.

words.meaning: Well-meaning and kindly; generous and charitable.
words.example: The benevolent nature of the Prophet was evident in his care for the poor and orphaned.

words.meaning: Having keen mental discernment and good judgement; wise and shrewd.
words.example: The sagacious counsel of the Prophet guided the companions through every difficulty.

words.meaning: Impossible to understand or comprehend fully.
words.example: The unfathomable love of the Prophet for his Ummah surpassed all human understanding.

words.meaning: In accordance with the highest standards of propriety; faultless.
words.example: The impeccable character of the Prophet left no room for any criticism.

words.meaning: To regard with great respect or reverence.
words.example: The scholars venerated the Prophet's teachings and transmitted them with utmost care.

words.meaning: Causing affection or warm regard; lovable.
words.example: The endearing habits of the Prophet endeared him to all who knew him.

words.meaning: The quality of being very generous or forgiving.
words.example: The magnanimity of the Prophet was legendary — he forgave even those who harmed him.
